transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
It's a burning when I pass water, and I'm needing to go much more often than usual. It's very uncomfortable and it's getting me down a bit, so I'd like to get it seen to.
When did you first notice the burning when you pass water and needing to go more often?
Oh, it's been about two weeks now.
Do you have any allergies to medicines, or have you ever had a bad reaction to one?
Yes, I'm allergic to trimethoprim — it gave me a nasty itchy rash.
Are you taking any medicines at the moment, either regularly or ones you've started or stopped recently?

Yes, I take levothyroxine 75 micrograms every morning, and alendronic acid 70 mg once a week for my thin bones. I also use a vaginal cream from the hospital twice a week, but I can't remember what it's called.
When you feel that burning when you pass water, where exactly do you feel it?
It's down below, in the water passage, when I'm actually passing water. The stinging is about 5 out of 10 — uncomfortable, but I'm managing.
Is there anything you've noticed that makes the burning or the need to go more often better or worse?
I can't say I've noticed anything that makes much difference, really — it's just there. I suppose going more often is because I feel I need to go, but that's about it.
Is the burning there every time you pass water, or does it come and go?
It's there most times I go, but it does vary a bit — sometimes stronger than others. It's not there all day, just when I'm passing water.
Is there anything else about your health in the past — like other ongoing health problems, past illnesses, operations, or times in hospital — that you’d like to add?
I've got an underactive thyroid, and I had a water infection about a year ago that was treated with antibiotics. That's about it as far as I can remember.
Is there anything else you've noticed going on alongside the burning and needing to go more often?
The water looks cloudy and smells stronger than usual, though I've not seen any blood. My niece hasn't noticed me being confused or anything like that either.
Are there any other medicines you take — anything at all, like tablets, creams, patches, or things you buy yourself — that we haven't talked about yet?
No, that's the lot — the levothyroxine, the alendronic acid, and the vaginal cream I can't remember the name of. I don't take anything else, and I don't buy anything myself.
Has this been getting in the way of your sleep at all?
Yes, it's disturbing my sleep quite a bit — I'm getting up three or four times in the night, when I'd usually only go once.
Is there anything else you've noticed that we haven't talked about yet?

Well, I have stopped going to the residents' coffee morning, as I'm worried I won't reach a toilet in time. I do think it's another water infection, and I'm hoping I can get some antibiotics before the weekend.
Is there anything else about your past health — other ongoing problems, past illnesses, operations, or times in hospital — that you’d like to add?
No, I don't think so — just the underactive thyroid and that water infection a year ago. Nothing else I can think of.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
